passages.text: Masters, supply your slaves with what is right and fair, since you know that you also have a Master in heaven.
passages.sermon:
Masters have authority over slaves.
Masters must give what is right to their slaves.
Masters must treat their slaves fairly.
Masters know they also have a Master.
Their Master is in heaven.
passages.original: Οἱ κύριοι τὸ δίκαιον καὶ τὴν ἰσότητα τοῖς δούλοις παρέχεσθε εἰδότες ὅτι καὶ ὑμεῖς ἔχετε Κύριον ἐν οὐρανῷ

passages.text: Devote yourselves to prayer, being watchful and thankful, as you pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, so that we may proclaim the mystery of Christ, for which I am in chains.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter while he was in chains for proclaiming Christ.
Paul asked believers to pray for him and his companions.
Devote yourselves to prayer.
Be watchful in your prayers.
Be thankful in your prayers.
Pray for us also.
Ask God to open a door for our message.
We want to speak the word of God.
We want to proclaim the mystery of Christ.
I am in chains because of this message.
passages.original: Τῇ προσευχῇ προσκαρτερεῖτε γρηγοροῦντες ἐν αὐτῇ ἐν εὐχαριστίᾳ προσευχόμενοι ἅμα καὶ περὶ ἡμῶν ἵνα ὁ Θεὸς ἀνοίξῃ ἡμῖν θύραν τοῦ λόγου λαλῆσαι τὸ μυστήριον τοῦ Χριστοῦ δι’ ὃ καὶ δέδεμαι

passages.text: Pray that I may declare it clearly, as I should.
passages.sermon:
Paul is the writer.
Paul is in chains for proclaiming Christ.
Paul asks for prayer.
Paul wants to speak about Christ.
Paul wants to speak clearly.
Paul wants to speak as he should.
Pray for Paul to declare the message clearly.
Pray for Paul to declare the message as he ought.
passages.original: ἵνα φανερώσω αὐτὸ ὡς δεῖ με λαλῆσαι

passages.text: Act wisely toward outsiders, redeeming the time.
passages.sermon: You must act with wisdom.\r\nYou must act this way toward people who are not part of the church.\r\nYou must make the best use of your time.
passages.original: Ἐν σοφίᾳ περιπατεῖτε πρὸς τοὺς ἔξω τὸν καιρὸν ἐξαγοραζόμενοι

passages.text: Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how to answer everyone.
passages.sermon: Let your speech always show grace.\r\nLet your words be seasoned with salt.\r\nThis will help you know how to answer each person.
passages.original: ὁ λόγος ὑμῶν πάντοτε ἐν χάριτι ἅλατι ἠρτυμένος εἰδέναι πῶς δεῖ ὑμᾶς ἑνὶ ἑκάστῳ ἀποκρίνεσθαι

passages.text: Tychicus will tell you all the news about me. He is a beloved brother, a faithful minister, and a fellow servant in the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Tychicus will tell you all the news about me.
Tychicus is a beloved brother.
Tychicus is a faithful minister.
Tychicus is a fellow servant in the Lord.
passages.original: Τὰ κατ’ ἐμὲ πάντα γνωρίσει ὑμῖν Τυχικὸς ὁ ἀγαπητὸς ἀδελφὸς καὶ πιστὸς διάκονος καὶ σύνδουλος ἐν Κυρίῳ

passages.text: I have sent him to you for this very purpose, that you may know about us, and that he may encourage your hearts.
passages.sermon:
Paul sent Tychicus to the believers in Colossae.
Tychicus is a beloved brother, a faithful minister, and a fellow servant in the Lord.
Paul sent Tychicus for a specific purpose.
Tychicus will tell the believers about Paul and his companions.
Tychicus will encourage the hearts of the believers.
passages.original: ὃν ἔπεμψα πρὸς ὑμᾶς εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦτο ἵνα γνῶτε τὰ περὶ ἡμῶν καὶ παρακαλέσῃ τὰς καρδίας ὑμῶν

passages.text: With him I am sending Onesimus, our faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They will tell you about everything here.
passages.sermon:
I am sending Onesimus with Tychicus.
Onesimus is a faithful brother.
He is a beloved brother.
He is one of you.
Tychicus and Onesimus will tell you everything that is happening here.
passages.original: σὺν Ὀνησίμῳ τῷ πιστῷ καὶ ἀγαπητῷ ἀδελφῷ ὅς ἐστιν ἐξ ὑμῶν πάντα ὑμῖν γνωρίσουσιν τὰ ὧδε

passages.text: My fellow prisoner Aristarchus sends you greetings, as does Mark the cousin of Barnabas. You have already received instructions about him: If he comes to you, welcome him.
passages.sermon:
Aristarchus is my fellow prisoner.
Aristarchus sends you greetings.
Mark is the cousin of Barnabas.
Mark also sends you greetings.
You have already received instructions about Mark.
If Mark comes to you, welcome him.
passages.original: Ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Ἀρίσταρχος ὁ συναιχμάλωτός μου καὶ Μᾶρκος ὁ ἀνεψιὸς Βαρνάβα περὶ οὗ ἐλάβετε ἐντολάς ἐὰν ἔλθῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς δέξασθε αὐτόν

passages.text: Jesus, who is called Justus, also sends greetings. These are the only Jews among my fellow workers for the kingdom of God, and they have been a comfort to me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is also called Justus.
He sends you greetings.
He is a Jew.
He is one of my fellow workers for the kingdom of God.
There are only a few Jews who work with me for God's kingdom.
These men have comforted me.
passages.original: καὶ Ἰησοῦς ὁ λεγόμενος Ἰοῦστος οἱ ὄντες ἐκ περιτομῆς οὗτοι μόνοι συνεργοὶ εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ οἵτινες ἐγενήθησάν μοι παρηγορία

passages.text: Epaphras, who is one of you and a servant of Christ Jesus, sends you greetings. He is always wrestling in prayer for you, so that you may stand mature and fully assured in the full will of God.
passages.sermon:
Epaphras sends you greetings.
Epaphras is one of you.
Epaphras is a servant of Christ Jesus.
Epaphras always wrestles in prayer for you.
He prays so that you may stand mature.
He prays so that you may be fully assured in all the will of God.
passages.original: Ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Ἐπαφρᾶς ὁ ἐξ ὑμῶν δοῦλος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ πάντοτε ἀγωνιζόμενος ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐν ταῖς προσευχαῖς ἵνα σταθῆτε τέλειοι καὶ πεπληροφορημένοι ἐν παντὶ θελήματι τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: For I testify about him that he goes to great pains for you and for those at Laodicea and Hierapolis.
passages.sermon:
I speak about Epaphras now.
Epaphras is a servant of Christ Jesus.
He is one of you.
I testify about Epaphras.
He works very hard for you.
He also works very hard for those in Laodicea.
He works very hard for those in Hierapolis.
passages.original: μαρτυρῶ γὰρ αὐτῷ ὅτι ἔχει πολὺν πόνον ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν καὶ τῶν ἐν Λαοδικείᾳ καὶ τῶν ἐν Ἱερα‿ πόλει

passages.text: Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas send you greetings.
passages.sermon:
Luke is a physician.
Luke is beloved.
Luke sends you greetings.
Demas also sends you greetings.
passages.original: Ἀσπάζεται ὑμᾶς Λουκᾶς ὁ ἰατρὸς ὁ ἀγαπητὸς καὶ Δημᾶς

passages.text: Greet the brothers in Laodicea, as well as Nympha and the church that meets at her house.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this letter.
Paul gives instructions to the believers in Colossae.
Paul tells them to greet the brothers in Laodicea.
Paul tells them to greet Nympha.
Paul tells them to greet the church that meets at Nympha’s house.
passages.original: Ἀσπάσασθε τοὺς ἐν Λαοδικείᾳ ἀδελφοὺς καὶ Νύμφαν καὶ τὴν κατ’ οἶκον αὐτῆς ἐκκλησίαν

passages.text: After this letter has been read among you, make sure that it is also read in the church of the Laodiceans, and that you in turn read the letter from Laodicea.
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the church in Colossae.
Paul wanted the believers in Colossae to read his letter.
Paul told them to share his letter with the church in Laodicea.
Paul told them to make sure the Laodiceans also read his letter.
Paul told the Colossians to read the letter from Laodicea as well.
passages.original: Καὶ ὅταν ἀναγνωσθῇ παρ’ ὑμῖν ἡ ἐπιστολή ποιήσατε ἵνα καὶ ἐν τῇ Λαοδικέων ἐκκλησίᾳ ἀναγνωσθῇ καὶ τὴν ἐκ Λαοδικείας ἵνα καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀναγνῶτε

passages.text: Tell Archippus: “See to it that you complete the ministry you have received in the Lord.”
passages.sermon:
Paul wrote this letter to the church.
Paul addressed the believers in Colossae.
Paul gave a message for Archippus.
Paul said, “Tell Archippus this.”
Archippus received a ministry from the Lord.
Paul told Archippus to pay attention to his ministry.
Paul told Archippus to complete his ministry.
passages.original: Καὶ εἴπατε Ἀρχίππῳ Βλέπε τὴν διακονίαν ἣν παρέλαβες ἐν Κυρίῳ ἵνα αὐτὴν πληροῖς

passages.text: This greeting is in my own hand—Paul. Remember my chains. Grace be with you.
passages.sermon:
Paul writes this greeting with his own hand.
Paul is the author of this letter.
Paul is in chains.
Remember Paul’s chains.
Grace is with you.
passages.original: Ὁ ἀσπασμὸς τῇ ἐμῇ χειρὶ Παύλου Μνημονεύετέ μου τῶν δεσμῶν Ἡ χάρις μεθ’ ὑμῶν
